data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient to correlated failure than a large redundant service because it leverages 'Cognitive and Substrate Diversity' to break the homogeneity required for systemic collapse.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services converge on a 'Shadow Monolith' by using the same managed cloud substrate (e.g., all on AWS us-east-1), rendering organizational independence irrelevant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The services are coupled via a critical shared dependency (e.g., a single global DNS provider or Auth0) that introduces a hidden single point of failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"While a large service increases redundancy (more nodes), it typically does so through homogeneity (identical software/config), creating a massive attack surface for a single latent bug. A decentralized network introduces variance in operator psychology (SCR_009), software versions, and underlying infrastructure (SCR_002), ensuring that a trigger affecting one service is unlikely to be compatible with the specific state of all others.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
